open_findings.claim: AC-4 defines 'no field option' as none of the options being present, but the test plan never checks an empty-string option (--title '' or --due ''), so a build that tests truthiness instead of presence passes.
open_findings.failure_scenario: A build treats `edit 1 --title ''` as no field and prints 'nothing to edit' (or treats --due '' as absent) instead of the required blank-title / invalid due date error; both exit 2, so the only visible difference is the stderr text, which no test checks for the empty string.

open_findings.claim: The --due, --no-due and --priority success tests run only on bare tasks, so nothing checks that these edits leave the task's other keys (tags, title, done, id) and other tasks untouched.
open_findings.failure_scenario: An edit_task that rebuilds the dict on --priority/--due, or drops tags when it deletes a key, passes every success test. A task with tags and a due date loses its tags on `edit 1 --priority normal` and no test fails. Only the --title test uses a full task.

open_findings.claim: The core no-mutation test pairs a valid title with each bad value, so it never catches a partial edit where a valid priority or due is applied before a later field fails. It also never tests a combined successful edit.
open_findings.failure_scenario: edit_task validates the title first, applies priority, then validates due. `edit_task(tasks, 1, priority='low', due='nope')` raises after mutating priority. The CLI tests cannot see this because the file is not saved on error. The core test never uses priority with a bad due, so it passes.

open_findings.claim: No test covers the order 'unknown id before no-field' (edit with an unknown id and no option), which AC-4 and the plan's risks state.
open_findings.failure_scenario: If edit_task checked 'nothing to edit' before looking up the id, `edit 99` would print `error: nothing to edit` instead of `error: no task with id 99` and every test would still pass, because the unknown-id cases always pass --title or --priority.

gaps.detail: No test applies several valid options in one edit (e.g. `edit 1 --title X --no-due --priority low`, or --title with --due and --priority). Add a CLI test in tests/test_edit.py checking all fields change together and the other keys (done, tags) and other tasks stay intact.

AC-4 says an unknown id is reported before value errors, but `edit 99 --due 2026-12-01 --no-due` (unknown id with the due/no-due conflict) is untested. In core.edit_task the due/no-due check could move before _find unnoticed. Add this case to test_ac4_no_field_and_unknown_id_are_errors, expecting 'error: no task with id 99'. (The `edit 99` no-option case is already finding tests-1.)

Strictness of --priority and --due inputs is not pinned by any test: `--priority HIGH`, `--priority ' high'`, `--priority ''`, and `--due ' 2026-12-01'` or a non-ASCII-digit date are rejected by the PRIORITIES membership check and by parse_date, but only urgent, 2026-02-30, abc and the empty due string are tested. Add parametrized invalid-priority and invalid-due cases expecting the exact 'error: invalid priority: X' / 'error: invalid due date: X' and an unchanged file.
